title: Catalytic pyrolysis of HDPE over ZSM-5 in a fixed-bed reactor
text: Catalytic pyrolysis of HDPE was investigated in a fixed-bed reactor over a ZSM-5 zeolite catalyst. At 500 °C and a residence time of 30 min, pyrolysis of HDPE with ZSM-5 achieved a liquid oil yield of 72 wt%. The addition of the catalyst reduced the wax content and increased aromatic hydrocarbons in the oil. Increasing the temperature above 600 °C decreased the liquid yield because of secondary cracking. These results demonstrate that catalytic pyrolysis is a promising route for HDPE waste valorisation.

title: Pyrolysis of mixed LDPE and polypropylene waste for fuel production
text: Pyrolysis of mixed LDPE and polypropylene waste was studied for waste-to-energy applications. At 450 °C for 60 min without a catalyst, pyrolysis produced a liquid oil yield of 58 wt% from LDPE. Polypropylene pyrolysis may yield lower oil quality, suggesting that feedstock composition could influence fuel properties. The calorific value of the pyrolysis oil was comparable to diesel, indicating potential for energy recovery. Long-term engine performance remains unclear and requires further investigation.

title: Glycolysis-based depolymerization of PET as a chemical recycling route
text: Glycolysis-based depolymerization of PET was evaluated as a chemical recycling route. Using a zinc acetate catalyst at 190 °C for 2 h, depolymerization of PET achieved 95% monomer conversion to BHET. Chemical recycling of PET through glycolysis improved monomer purity compared with mechanical recycling. However, catalyst recovery was inefficient and the economic viability of chemical recycling is uncertain. Further pilot-scale studies are needed.

title: Enzymatic biodegradation of PET film by engineered PETase
text: Enzymatic biodegradation of PET film was examined using engineered PETase. At 40 °C over 72 h, PETase degraded 30% of amorphous PET film. Biodegradation of PET decreased substantially for highly crystalline PET, which limits the enzyme performance. The results suggest that thermal pretreatment might enhance biodegradation, although the mechanism is not fully understood.

title: Microplastics in freshwater sediments near urban waste sites
text: Microplastics were quantified in freshwater sediments near urban waste sites. Microplastics concentrations reached 1200 particles per kg and were dominated by polystyrene and polypropylene fragments. Exposure to microplastics reduced the growth of freshwater invertebrates in laboratory tests. The long-term environmental impact of microplastics remains inconclusive because field data are limited.

title: UV photodegradation of polystyrene and nanoplastic formation
text: Photodegradation of polystyrene under UV irradiation generated nanoplastics in aqueous suspension. After 120 h of UV exposure at 25 °C, photodegradation of polystyrene produced nanoplastics smaller than 200 nm. Photodegradation increased the surface oxidation of polystyrene particles. Nanoplastics may enhance the transport of organic pollutants, but toxicity effects are unclear.

title: Mechanical recycling of PET bottles in a circular economy framework
text: Mechanical recycling of PET bottles was assessed within a circular economy framework. Repeated reprocessing cycles reduced the intrinsic viscosity of recycled PET, decreasing mechanical strength after five cycles. Mechanical recycling improved recycling efficiency when sorting quality was high, achieving 85% material recovery. Policy incentives could support a circular economy for plastics, suggesting that collection systems are critical.

title: Steam gasification of plastic waste for hydrogen-rich syngas
text: Gasification of plastic waste was investigated for syngas production. At 800 °C with steam, gasification of polypropylene and LDPE produced a hydrogen-rich syngas with 45 vol% H2. A nickel catalyst increased hydrogen yield and reduced tar formation. Gasification demonstrated higher energy recovery than incineration, supporting waste-to-energy deployment. Catalyst deactivation was observed and may limit long-term operation.

title: Catalysed cracking of polyolefin waste over Y-zeolite
text: Catalysed cracking of polyolefin waste over a Y-zeolite catalyst was compared with thermal cracking. At 450 °C for 45 min, catalysed cracking of polypropylene increased gasoline-range hydrocarbons to 60 wt%. The presence of PVC in the feed released HCl and reduced catalyst activity. Dechlorination pretreatment improved cracking performance, although its effect on environmental impact is unclear.

title: Review of plastic waste management and sustainable recycling pathways
text: A review of plastic waste management strategies compared sustainable recycling pathways. Pyrolysis was reported to reduce greenhouse gas emissions relative to landfilling in some life cycle assessments, while other studies found that pyrolysis increased emissions due to energy demand. Chemical recycling may complement mechanical recycling for mixed plastics, suggesting that a combination of routes could advance sustainable recycling and improve recycling efficiency. Results are inconclusive due to inconsistent system boundaries.
